---
title: "Rule graph — spring, thin opaque edges"
output:
  html_document: { toc: true, toc_float: true, theme: flatly }
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 8, dpi = 105)
suppressMessages(devtools::load_all("..", quiet = TRUE))
set.seed(21)
```

```{r data}
acts6 <- c("read", "video", "quiz", "forum", "submit", "review")
acts12 <- c(acts6, "search", "annotate", "bookmark", "chat", "upload", "revise")
mk <- function(acts, n = 40) do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n), function(s) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(1:5, function(les) {
    k <- sample(3:6, 1)
    data.frame(student = paste0("s", s), lesson = paste0("L", les),
               when = seq_len(k), what = sample(acts, k, replace = TRUE),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}))
fit <- dynarules(mk(acts6), actor="student", action="what", time="when",
                 session="lesson", unit="session",
                 min_support=0.05, min_confidence=0.25, min_lift=0)
fit12 <- dynarules(mk(acts12), actor="student", action="what", time="when",
                   session="lesson", unit="session",
                   min_support=0.02, min_confidence=0.2, min_lift=0)
draw <- function(net, title=NULL) { cograph::splot(net, title=title); rule_key(net) }
```

Defaults now: **spring**, node size **c(4, 15)**, edges **thin (0.5) and fully
opaque (alpha = 1)**.

# 1. The new default

```{r}
draw(as_network(fit, level="rule", top=20), "spring, thin opaque edges")
```

# 2. Old hazy edges vs new

## Old — cograph default alpha 0.8, weight-scaled width

```{r}
draw(as_network(fit, level="rule", top=20, edge_width=NULL, edge_alpha=0.8),
     "edge_alpha = 0.8, width scaled by weight (the hazy look)")
```

## New — alpha 1, uniform 0.5

```{r}
draw(as_network(fit, level="rule", top=20), "edge_alpha = 1, edge_width = 0.5")
```

# 3. How thin?

```{r}
for (w in c(0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 1.2)) {
  draw(as_network(fit, level="rule", top=20, edge_width=w),
       paste("edge_width =", w))
}
```

# 4. spring vs gephi

```{r}
for (lay in c("spring", "gephi_fr")) {
  draw(as_network(fit, level="rule", top=20, layout=lay),
       paste("layout =", lay))
}
```

# 5. 12 items, both layouts

```{r}
for (lay in c("spring", "gephi_fr")) {
  draw(as_network(fit12, level="rule", top=25, layout=lay),
       paste("12 items, layout =", lay))
}
```

# 6. Colour ramps

```{r}
for (pal in c("sequential", "diverging", "greys")) {
  draw(as_network(fit, level="rule", top=20, palette=pal),
       paste("palette =", pal))
}
```

# 7. Sequential rules

```{r}
sfit <- dynarules(mk(acts6), type="sequential", actor="student", action="what",
                  time="when", session="lesson", unit="session",
                  min_support=0.08, min_confidence=0.25, min_lift=0)
for (lay in c("spring", "gephi_fr")) {
  draw(as_network(sfit, level="rule", top=20, layout=lay),
       paste("sequential, layout =", lay))
}
```
